_note: The claims model holds each load-bearing proposition the book asserts, plus the AUDIT PREDICATE (`contradicted_by`) naming what prose would negate it. JUDGMENT-AUDIT BOUNDARY (DESIGN §4.2): the contradiction check is a SEMANTIC judgment-audit owned by a review gate, NOT a blocking lint; only the structural / schema checks (C1–C6 + the C7-drift freshness check) are mechanical and may ever go blocking, and the watch-phrase surfacing lint (C7) stays AUDIT-ONLY FOREVER (a hit is a review candidate, never a verdict). REFLEXIVE PAYOFF (DESIGN §4.3): the two aides — the pre-edit consult (`catalog.py claims <chapter>`, the CONSTRAINT that aims the editing agent away from the drift) and the watch-phrase lint plus judgment-audit (the SENSOR that catches it after) — instantiate the book's own Alignment Thesis on its own manuscript. The model does not merely record the constraint/sensor distinction; it applies it to the book's prose.

claims.statement: The apparatus is the review: the environment holds every change to standard, not per-change human inspection.
distinguishes: the governing apparatus — constraints, sensors, validators, gates hold every change to standard
per-change human inspection — re-reading each change by hand
claims.contradicted_by: Prose treating recurring per-change human review as the reliability mechanism, rather than the governing apparatus that holds every change automatically.
claims.anchor: part1.md names 'The apparatus is the review' a major book claim, but no chapter yet lands it as a dedicated named formulation — the review-replacement slogan's net-subtractive fix-wave will canonicalize it. Homed at the soft/hard-layer argument (the-soft-layer-guides-the-hard-layer-holds); it is the Alignment-Principle consequence of oversight-does-not-scale.

claims.statement: Churn is the symptom; its causes are the three not-knowings, and every technique attacks a cause.
distinguishes: churn — the symptom
the three not-knowings — the causes
claims.contradicted_by: Treating churn as the root problem to fix directly, or a technique aimed at the symptom rather than a cause.
claims.anchor: Preface premise: churn is the symptom; the causes are the three not-knowings, and each technique attacks a cause.

claims.statement: A quality goal splits into a constraint that prevents the error and a sensor that observes it.
distinguishes: a constraint — prevents the error
a sensor — observes it after the fact and produces evidence
claims.contradicted_by: Conflating the roles — calling a sensor a validator, or treating a preventer as a detector.
claims.anchor: Preface Alignment Principle + 3.3 prevention-and-observation: a quality goal splits into a constraint (prevent) and a sensor (observe); the sensor produces evidence, a validator judges it.

claims.statement: Each governance conversion is engineering capital: it lowers the future cost of change while it stays fit.
claims.contradicted_by: Treating more governance as monotonically better, or accumulation that raises apparatus without lowering future reasoning (bureaucracy that never compounds, or capital left unretired past its fit).
claims.anchor: Part 6: each conversion is engineering capital, not technical debt; compounding is the positive dual of churn, bounded by fit (bureaucracy and depreciation are the two ways it stops).

claims.statement: Velocity exposes the unforeseeable failure; judgment converts each recurring one into a mechanism.
claims.contradicted_by: Prescribing up-front enumeration of all obligations as the method, or per-instance patching without retiring the class.
claims.anchor: Preface 'three ways' close + 2.3 ex-post: velocity surfaces the unforeseeable failure; judgment converts each recurrence into infrastructure.

claims.statement: MAGE's claim is about maintenance (model and code kept equal under drift gates), not authoring direction.
distinguishes: maintenance — model and code equal under drift gates
authoring direction — model→code or code→model as the rule
claims.contradicted_by: Prose stating MAGE prescribes model→code (or code→model) as its own authoring direction — the drift the 3.1 scope-box fix corrected.
claims.anchor: Preface Lineage touchstone: 'Its claim is about maintenance, not authorship … whichever artifact came first.' 3.1 scope box (post-fix): 'bound to the code — derived in either direction, gated either way.'

claims.statement: A model earns its keep twice: it solves the agent's context problem and it holds quality.
claims.contradicted_by: Framing models as only a context-savings, or only a quality tool.
claims.anchor: Preface Lineage: models 'earn their keep twice.' 3.1 and 2.2 develop both the context and the quality wins.

claims.statement: The fleet is bounded by reasoning power and context window, not Brooks's N² communication overhead.
distinguishes: reasoning power and context window — the real bounds
Brooks N² communication overhead
claims.contradicted_by: Blaming coordination / communication overhead; OR treating the context window as the sole bound, ignoring reasoning capacity.
watch_phrases: scaling limit is the context window
claims.anchor: Preface premise + 6.0: the fleet hits churn, not Brooks's N² wall; both reasoning capacity and the context window are engineered against.

claims.statement: Governance is not a point on the velocity–oversight dial; it changes what reliability is made of.
distinguishes: a point on the velocity↔oversight dial
changes what reliability is made of — pay per-class-of-failure
claims.contradicted_by: Prose placing governance as a midpoint / balance on the speed-safety dial (the resolved 'midway' framing).
claims.anchor: Preface 'three ways to run a fleet': 'Governance is not a point on that line' — it changes what reliability is made of, paying per class of failure.

claims.statement: Part 5 is the grounding case the method was derived from, never its proof.
claims.contradicted_by: Prose presenting Part 5 or DocAble as proof of the method or its principles — 'the proof', 'proves the method' — rather than as the grounding case / worked case / evidence base.
claims.anchor: Preface caution: 'This is a single-case field report … read it as an observation from that case rather than a measured law.'

claims.statement: Engineering discipline must be mechanized, not remembered: push it into tooling so correctness never depends on recall.
claims.contradicted_by: Relying on an agent or human remembering, or being careful, as the enforcement.
claims.anchor: Preface premise (SE-at-Google touchstone): discipline is mechanized into tooling, not left to memory or care.

claims.statement: A model's value is both its structure and the invariants it lets you enforce.
distinguishes: the structure — records, edges, state machines — that names the parts and gives tools something to read
the checked invariants — the predicates a gate holds true, which complete the model's value rather than replace the schema
claims.contradicted_by: Prose that treats a model's schema ALONE as its whole value — counting an unchecked structure as a finished model — OR that dismisses the schema as worthless, denying that the structure carries value the invariants complete.
claims.anchor: 3.1 'The coherence triangle': the model provides two kinds of value — the schema names the parts, and the checked invariants (each earned from a failure) complete it; the invariants and gate complete the schema's value rather than replacing it.

claims.statement: A model is not a governance mechanism until something reads or enforces it.
claims.contradicted_by: Prose counting a bare model — read by nothing, enforced by nothing — as a governance mechanism.
claims.anchor: 3.3 'What counts as a mechanism': a structured model on disk aims nobody — the model supplies the policy; the mechanism that reads or enforces it supplies the holding.

claims.statement: Models are the language of engineering; software could not afford them until agents cut sync cost.
claims.contradicted_by: Framing models as a nice-to-have or a software-specific trick rather than engineering's common language.
claims.anchor: Preface universal-language touchstone + 6.0 'models as a common language of mature engineering' + conclusion.

claims.statement: Modeling and Alignment treat different but not independent engineering problems, resting on one shared conception of acceptable realization.
claims.contradicted_by: Collapsing the two principles into one, or denying that Alignment rests on any conception of acceptable realization — treating it as acting without one.
claims.anchor: Preface 'What the method turned out to be': the two principles solve different problems but are not independent — each rests on the same underlying conception of acceptable realization, which Modeling externalizes and Alignment gives authority.

claims.statement: Building with an agent is running a printer, not a coder: suspect the instructions before the agent's capability.
claims.contradicted_by: Treating a bad output as a fixed capability ceiling by reflex, without first examining the instructions, representation, task boundary, or environment.
claims.anchor: Preface through-line + 1.1 the-printer / whose-fault-is-it: the agent is a printer; a bad output is first evidence about the instructions, representation, task boundary, or environment, not by reflex a fixed capability ceiling.

claims.statement: Host-specific resource limits live in a per-host scheduler profile, not by forking the execution graph.
distinguishes: a per-host scheduler profile — host limits set as scheduling parameters against one shared graph
forking the execution graph — a separate invariant-DAG edited per host
claims.contradicted_by: Prose that models a host's resource limits by editing or forking the execution graph itself, rather than as a per-host scheduling profile over one shared graph.
claims.anchor: The Physical View (3.5/3.6): host-specific resource limits are a per-host scheduler profile — `plan = plan_for(host_profile)` — over one shared invariant-DAG, not a forked graph per host. No chapter yet lands 'profile edit, not graph edit' as a dedicated named formulation; the profile-edit-not-graph-edit slogan's fix-wave canonicalizes it. A Modeling-Principle instance: the deployment view is a model (a scheduling profile), not an edit to the executable graph.

claims.statement: The lifecycle stays intact and gains no phases; only the developer's implementation seat moves to the fleet.
distinguishes: the developer's seat moves to the fleet
the lifecycle itself changes
claims.contradicted_by: Claiming agents replace the whole lifecycle, or that the lifecycle itself changes.
claims.anchor: 6.5 implications-for-se: SDLC → SELC — the human keeps requirements/spec/design/validation; only the coding seat moves to the fleet.

claims.statement: This is a single-case field report; its numbers are observations from one system, not measured laws.
claims.contradicted_by: Stating a number as a general or measured law across systems.
claims.anchor: scope conditions: a single-case field report; the numbers are observations from one system, not measured laws — the contribution is mechanism.

claims.statement: Mechanisms sit on a soft-to-hard spectrum; push a recurring failure as far toward hard enforcement as possible.
distinguishes: a soft mechanism — aims the agent
a hard mechanism — holds the line
claims.contradicted_by: Treating a convention or brief as equivalent to a lint or gate, or claiming a convention 'holds the line'.
claims.anchor: 4.1 'From soft to hard' (governance-conversion method, re-homed to the-mage-workflow in round-6) + 2.3: guidance aims, machinery holds; a recurring soft-rule failure moves right.

claims.statement: One source of truth, kept equal either way; a parallel snapshot is a second source that drifts.
distinguishes: one source of truth kept equal either way
a parallel hand-updated snapshot — a second source
claims.contradicted_by: Endorsing a model kept as a separate hand-updated artifact (a second source), or asserting one fixed derivation direction as the rule.
claims.anchor: 3.1 scope box: 'a second representation is a snapshot — it drifts the moment the code moves.' Preface: the map kept in sync 'for cents.'

claims.statement: Churn's recurring causes are weak representation (knowledge rediscovered) and weak authority (obligations re-inspected).
claims.contradicted_by: Enumerating a fixed count of churn causes unrelated to weak representation or weak authority.
claims.anchor: Preface 'What changed': churn is what happens when knowledge or obligations must be paid for again — weak representation forces rediscovery, weak authority forces repeated inspection.
